Assume AC. Let $h>0$, $x,y\in\mathbb R$, and let $W$ be a standard scalar
Brownian motion on $[0,h]$. The **scalar Brownian bridge from $x$ to $y$ over
duration $h$** is the continuous Gaussian process
$$B^{x,y,h}_t=x+\frac{t}{h}(y-x)+W_t-\frac{t}{h}W_h, \qquad 0\le t\le h.$$
It starts at $x$ and ends at $y$. Its law does not depend on which Brownian
motion is used: Brownian increment laws determine its finite-dimensional laws,
and continuity determines its path law from rational coordinate evaluations
using [[lem-borel-sigma-algebra-of-continuous-path-space-is-generated-by-coordinates]]
and [[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]]. The endpoint-conditional and restriction-density
properties are established separately on the A page.

Let $d\ge1$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $P_C(y)$ be the unique nearest point in $C$ to $y$, whose existence and uniqueness are [[thm-nearest-point-in-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set]]. For $x\in C$, set
$$N_C(x)=\{n\in\mathbb R^d:\langle n,z-x\rangle\le0\text{ for every }z\in C\};$$
for $x\notin C$, set $N_C(x)=\varnothing$. On $C$ this is the outward normal cone of [[def-kkt-residual-and-normal-cone]]. The projection variational inequality of [[lem-projection-onto-a-closed-convex-set-has-the-variational-inequality]] says $P_C(y)=p$ exactly when $p\in C$ and $y-p\in N_C(p)$.

For $T>0$, a solution of the projected contact dynamics with forcing $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$ and initial state $x_0\in C$ is an absolutely continuous map $x:[0,T]\to C$ satisfying
$$f(t,x(t))-\dot x(t)\in N_C(x(t))\quad\text{for almost every }t\in[0,T].$$
Equivalently, $\dot x(t)+N_C(x(t))\ni f(t,x(t))$. For an integer $N\ge1$, put $h=T/N$, $t_k=kh$, and define the exact explicit projection Euler nodes by
$$x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)\bigr),\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1,$$
starting from $x_0$. Its affine interpolant joins consecutive nodes linearly on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1}]$.

For a map $x:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^d$, **absolutely continuous** means that each coordinate is absolutely continuous in the scalar sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]], and $\dot x(t)$ is the vector of coordinate derivatives, from [[def-derivative]], wherever they all exist. The solution condition requires a Lebesgue-null set $N\subseteq[0,T]$ such that for every $t\notin N$ all coordinate derivatives exist and the displayed inclusion holds. Here **almost every $t$** is relative to Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ from [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]], with the convention of [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]].

$$\log_N(P_h)=\sum_{k=1}^{N+1}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}(P_h-I)^k,$$

A **smooth hybrid ODE system** on a finite horizon $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$ and positive integer state dimension $d\ge1$, consists of a finite mode set $M$, an open state-time domain $D_m\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ and a $C^1$ vector field $f_m:D_m\to\mathbb R^d$ for each $m\in M$, a finite set of directed transitions $(m,n)$, and for each transition a $C^1$ scalar guard $g_{mn}$, a declared crossing orientation $\sigma_{mn}\in\{-1,+1\}$, and a $C^1$ reset map $R_{mn}$ defined on a neighborhood of the guard points and taking values in the next mode's state domain. Here $C^1$ has the meaning in [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. In mode $m$, a trajectory is a solution of the first-order initial-value problem $y'=f_m(t,y)$ in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. It follows that mode only until the selected event time.

An **event time** for transition $(m,n)$ is a time $\tau$ at which $g_{mn}(\tau,y(\tau))=0$ and the guard crosses in its declared direction, meaning $\sigma_{mn}\frac{d}{dt}g_{mn}(t,y(t))|_{t=\tau}>0$. It is **transverse** with margin $\nu>0$ on a bracket when $\sigma_{mn}\frac{d}{dt}g_{mn}(t,y(t))\ge\nu$ throughout that bracket. At an event, the state changes from $y(\tau^-)$ to $R_{mn}(\tau,y(\tau^-))$ and the mode changes from $m$ to $n$. A **deterministic event-priority rule** is a fixed total order on the finite outgoing transition set of each mode; if several enabled guards vanish at exactly the same first time, the least transition in that order is selected.

A hybrid trajectory has a **finite separated event list** on $[0,T]$ when it has finitely many event times $0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_N<T$ and some $\delta>0$ with $\tau_{j+1}-\tau_j\ge\delta$ for each adjacent pair. The definition does not assert that a solution exists, that an event is detected, or that the event list is finite. Those are separate hypotheses or conclusions.

Input: an open domain $U$, a Hermitian response matrix map $F:U\to\mathbb H_n$,
and its gapped occupied-projector map $\Phi$ from
[[def-self-consistent-projector-response-map]]; a nonempty complete invariant
set $K\subseteq U\cap\mathcal P_r$ with $\Phi(K)\subseteq K$ and certified
contraction factor $0\le q<1$; an initial projector $P_0\in K$; a certified
initial error bound $E_0\ge\|P_0-P_*\|_F$ for the unique fixed point $P_*$;
residual tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$; finite update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$;
memory $m\ge1$; coefficient cap $C\ge1$; a Hermitian eigensolver that, for a
matrix $M$, returns a certified ordered spectrum and occupied projector when
the $r$th gap is strict, a certified no-gap result, or a failure to certify the
spectrum; an approximate response evaluator that at $X\in K$ returns
$\widetilde\Phi(X)\in K$ and $\eta(X)\ge0$ with
$\|\widetilde\Phi(X)-\Phi(X)\|_F\le\eta(X)$, or a failure status; and a
constrained least-squares solver that either returns the certified global
minimizer with the minimum-norm tie-break for the residuals and cap $C$, or
reports failure. Every called solver returns one of its specified results.

The terminal output is $(P_k,\texttt{status},b,k)$, where $P_k$ is the current
projector and $b$ is its certified error bound. The current budget $E_k$
remains valid at gap, eigensolver, or invariance-certificate failure statuses.

For $k=0,\ldots,N$:

1. If no certified response evaluation is cached for $P_k$, compute $F(P_k)$ and call the eigensolver on it. If the eigensolver certifies no strict gap, return $(P_k,\texttt{gap-loss},E_k,k)$; if it fails to certify the spectrum, return $(P_k,\texttt{eigensolve-failure},E_k,k)$. With a certified strict gap, call the approximate response evaluator. If it fails, return $(P_k,\texttt{eigensolve-failure},E_k,k)$. Cache $(F(P_k),\widetilde\Phi(P_k),\eta(P_k))$ at exactly $P_k$. Whether this evaluation is new or cached, check that the certified baseline output belongs to $K$; if not, return $(P_k,\texttt{invariance-certificate-failure},E_k,k)$. Retain the current pair $(P_k,F(P_k))$ for this proposal step. Set $\bar\rho_k=\|P_k-\widetilde\Phi(P_k)\|_F+\eta(P_k)$. If $\bar\rho_k\le\varepsilon$, return $(P_k,\texttt{residual-tolerance-met},\bar\rho_k/(1-q),k)$.
2. If $k=N$, return $(P_k,\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted},E_k,k)$.
3. Call [[alg-capped-diis-projector-proposal]] with the up-to-$m-1$ preceding stored pairs, the current pair $(P_k,F(P_k))$, the constrained least-squares solver, the eigensolver, $m$, and $C$. For a candidate $Y$, certify $Y\in K$, compute $F(Y)$, certify its strict gap with the eigensolver, and obtain one approximate response evaluation $\widetilde\Phi(Y)$ with error $\eta(Y)$. Accept $Y$ only if all certificates succeed and
$$\frac{\|Y-\widetilde\Phi(Y)\|_F+\eta(Y)}{1-q}\le qE_k.$$
If accepted, set $P_{k+1}=Y$ and $E_{k+1}=qE_k$.
4. If step 3 does not accept a candidate for any reason, use the certified baseline evaluation already obtained and checked in step 1. In particular, this includes a least-squares failure, coefficient-cap or affine-constraint failure, failed candidate $K$-membership, failed candidate gap, failed candidate response-error certificate, or failed candidate fixed-point residual test. Set $P_{k+1}=\widetilde\Phi(P_k)$ and $E_{k+1}=qE_k+\eta(P_k)$.
5. Append the current pair $(P_k,F(P_k))$ to the preceding-iterate history, retaining at most the newest $m-1$ preceding pairs. If step 3 accepted $Y$, cache its certified evaluation $(F(Y),\widetilde\Phi(Y),\eta(Y))$ as the next iteration's current evaluation; if the baseline branch was used, evaluate its new iterate when the next loop begins. Never attach a response matrix evaluated at one density to a different density.

The DIIS commutator objective is only a proposal score. Acceptance uses the
separate fixed-point residual $\|Y-\Phi(Y)\|_F$ with its additive eigensolver
error certificate. The algorithm makes no unconditional success claim: finite
budget exhaustion and each certificate failure are explicit outcomes.

$u_0=u_0(\theta,\xi_0),\qquad u_{k+1}=\Psi_k(u_k,\theta,\xi_{k+1})\quad(0\le k<N).$

$F_N(\theta,\xi):=\phi(u_N,\theta)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k(u_k,\theta),\qquad J_N(\theta):=\mathbb E[F_N(\theta,\xi)].$
Assume $F_N(\theta,\xi)$ is integrable for every $\theta\in U$, and that there is a nonnegative integrable random variable $M$ with $\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta,\xi)\|_2\le M$ for all $\theta\in U$ almost surely, while $\mathbb E\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta_0,\xi)\|_2^2<\infty$. $S_{k+1}=D_u\Psi_k\,S_k+D_\theta\Psi_k,$

$p_N=\nabla_u\phi(u_N,\theta),\qquad p_k=\nabla_u\ell_k(u_k,\theta)+(D_u\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}.$

$\Gamma_N=\nabla_\theta\phi+S_0^\mathsf T p_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left(\nabla_\theta\ell_k+(D_\theta\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}\right)$
